packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-12 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure statement
- Nothing in my context before reading (task instructions, PROMPT.md) proposed an identification or reading.
- While reading, I recognised the Latin as a familiar liturgical/biblical text. I did not consult any source. I have tried not to supply letters from memory: where a word is only partly visible I mark it with [ ], ? or [illegible]. Some expansions and word divisions in damaged spots may still be biased by that recognition. These are flagged with "(?)" below.
- I did nothing beyond the stated rules. Besides PROMPT.md and the images, I ran one `ls` on the two packet directories to get the image filenames. I did not open packet.json.

Images
- image-001.jpg: overview of face A. Two separate parchment strips on black card, with a colour checker and a cm scale. Upper strip pencil label "Stams, STA, Frg. 167-1r". Lower strip pencil label "Stams, STA, Frg. 167 2v" (read from image-004).
- image-002 and image-003: overlapping left/right tiles of the upper strip in image-001 (1r).
- image-004 and image-005: overlapping left/right tiles of the lower strip in image-001 (2v).
- image-006.jpg: overview of face B. Upper strip labelled "...Frg. 167-1v", lower strip labelled "...Frg. 167 2r" (the label is partly unclear in image-009 and may read "2v"; my best reading is "2r").
- image-007 and image-008: tiles of the upper strip in image-006 (1v).
- image-009 and image-010: tiles of the lower strip in image-006 (2r).
- All images loaded.

Layout survey (observations)
- Each strip is a horizontal cut-down fragment of about 11 x 4 cm, with 7 lines of a single text column. Line ends survive on the right, so the column is complete in width. The top and bottom are cut through the text block.
- Script: small Gothic textualis book hand in brown ink. Abbreviations are frequent: superscript strokes, "s" with a stroke for s(un)t, the tironian 7/& sign, q(uonia)m.
- Rubrication: red verse initials of one line height inside the line, at the start of each new sentence. On 1r there is a large red initial D about 4 lines high at the left, with the text indented beside it. On 2r a red M is set out in the left margin.
- No running titles, interlinear glosses or underlining are visible.
- The right margins of 1r (image-003) and 2r (image-010) carry faint brown writing in a different, smaller layout, about 6-8 short lines. It is too faded to read. It could be marginal annotation, offset, or ghost text from former use as binding waste. I cannot tell which from these images.
- The text reads as continuous prose verse divided by red initials. There is no visible separation into lemma and commentary.
- Tentative, text-based: the last line of 1r ends "super-" and the first line of 2r begins "gr...sse s(un)t". This suggests that strip 2 originally sat directly below strip 1 on the same face, and that strip 2 was mounted with its other side up relative to strip 1. This inference rests on the reading, not on physical evidence.

Areas selected: all seven lines of each of the four strip faces. These are short enough to transcribe entirely. Unread: the faded right-margin writing on 1r and 2r. A raking-light or UV image of those margins would be needed.

Conventions: () expansion; [ ] partly visible or damaged; ? uncertain; (red X) red initial.

--- Strip 1r: image-002 (left) + image-003 (right), overlapping. Line numbers follow the text lines of the strip, 1-7 from the top. ---
image-002/003 l.1  (red D, 4 lines high)[..]nabit[..] e[..] q(uonia)m(?) sperauer[unt?] me[o?]   [beginning before "nabit" is lost in the initial area; "meo/me" at line end is faint]
image-002/003 l.2  [.]e ne in furore(?) tuo arguas me[.]   [first letters damaged/stained; "me" at line end faint]
image-002/003 l.3  neq(ue) in ira tua corripias me. (red Q)uo(niam)
image-002/003 l.4  sagitte tue infixe s(un)t m(ichi). (et) confirmasti sup(er)
image-002/003 l.5  me manu(m) tua(m). (red N)on e(st) sanitas in carne mea
image-002/003 l.6  a facie ire tue. n(on) e(st) pax ossibus meis a facie
image-002/003 l.7  peccator(um) meor(um). (red Q)uo(niam) iniquitates mee super-
Right margin (image-003): about 7 short lines of faded writing [illegible].

--- Strip 2v: image-004 (left) + image-005 (right) ---
image-004/005 l.1  dies d(omi)ne d(eu)s m(eu)s. (red Q)uia dixi nequando sup(er)-
image-004/005 l.2  gaudeant m(ichi) inimici mei. (et) du(m) co(m)mouent(ur)
image-004/005 l.3  pedes mei sup(er) me magna locuti s(un)t. (red Q)uo(niam) ego
image-004/005 l.4  in flagella paratus su(m). et dolor m(eu)s in conspc(tu)   [written "inc(on)sp(e)c" with abbreviation strokes]
image-004/005 l.5  eius(?) meo semp(er). (red Q)uo(niam) iniquitate(m) mea(m) annu(n)tia-   [first word looks like "eiu"/"ctu"; "annuntia" partly obscured by a stain]
image-004/005 l.6  bo. (et) cogitabo p(ro) peccato meo. (red I)nimici aut(em)   [red I is faint]
image-004/005 l.7  mei uiuunt (et) confirmati s(un)t sup(er) me. (et) mul-
A small hole sits right of the l.5 line end. The edges are cut.

--- Strip 1v: image-007 (left) + image-008 (right). This face is heavily abraded and stained, especially the left-centre. ---
image-007/008 l.1  me erant de [illegible ~2 words: "p..." visible] [..]ret(?). et ui(m) faciebant qu[i/a]
image-007/008 l.2  querebant [illegible ~1-2 words] [..]ea(?). (red E)t q(ui) inquirebant ma-
image-007/008 l.3  la m(ichi) lo[..] [illegible ~1 word, "..ar.." visible] (et) dolos tota die me-
image-007/008 l.4  ditabant(ur?). (red E)[go?] [aut(em)? illegible] tamq(uam) surdus n(on) audie-   [red initial only partly preserved]
image-007/008 l.5  ba(m). (et) sic(ut) mu[t..] [illegible] ap(er)iens os suu(m). (red E)t fact(us) su(m)
image-007/008 l.6  sicut homo n(on) audiens [illegible, ? (et)] n(on) habens in ore su[o/e]   [written "inore"]
image-007/008 l.7  redargutiones. (red Q)uo(niam) in te d(omi)ne sp(er)aui. tu exau-   [the red initial is faint; "speraui" uncertain]

--- Strip 2r: image-009 (left) + image-010 (right) ---
image-009/010 l.1  gr[e?]sse(?) s(un)t caput meu(m). sic(ut) onus graue gra-   [first word abraded: "g", "r" and a final "-sse/-tse" are visible]
image-009/010 l.2  uate s(un)t sup(er) me. (red P)utruer(un)t (et) corrupte s(un)t
image-009/010 l.3  cicatrices mee. a facie insipientie mee.
image-009/010 l.4  (red M, in left margin)iser factus [su(m)?] (et) curuatus su(m) usq(ue) in finem. tota   [the word after "factus" is a small sign, perhaps "s(um)" or "&"]
image-009/010 l.5  die contristat(us) ingrediebar. (red Q)uo(niam) lumbi   [ingrediebar partly abraded]
image-009/010 l.6  mei impleti s(un)t illusionib(us). (et) n(on) e(st) sanitas in
image-009/010 l.7  carne mea. (red A)fflictus [su(m)?] (et) humiliat(us) su(m)[..]   [the line end is cut at the bottom edge and partly abraded]
Right margin (image-010): faded writing, about 5 lines, [illegible]. Possible letters on l.3 of the margin: "salue(?)".
Left margin (image-009): a hole beside l.5.

Limitations
- These are fragments only: about 7 lines per face, cut top and bottom. The original page format and the number of lines are unknown.
- Strip 1v is badly abraded in the left-centre. About 6-8 words there are unread.
- The strip/face pairing (which strip faces belong together physically) is taken from the pencil shelf labels and the two overviews. The 1r→2r continuity is a text-based inference only.
- The marginal faint writing on 1r and 2r is unread.
